text: January the fifteenth, two thousand nine. US Airways Flight fifteen forty-nine takes off from LaGuardia, bound for Charlotte. It's climbing through about two thousand eight hundred feet when the crew sees birds. Canada geese. Big ones, several kilograms each. A jet engine's front fan spins thousands of times a minute, and swallows a huge amount of air. Engines are tested by firing birds into them. But these geese were heavier than the birds these engines had to keep running after. Geese go into both engines. Blades and cores are damaged, and both engines lose almost all their thrust. Behind the fan sits the core, where fuel burns. Wreck the blades in front of it, and the airflow breaks down. The engine can't keep itself running. At least the engines' casings did their job. Broken parts stayed inside, instead of flying into the wings and cabin.
